title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad-lena-2026-04-21
content:
Quick notes / running log — attempting to triage repeated 401s and intermittent 429 spikes seen 2026-04-20 -> 2026-04-21. Mostly reproduces for a particular customer token and one internal integration. Scratchy, chronological, commands & hypotheses.

Summary / symptoms:
- Customer reported batches of requests returning 401 (invalid_api_key) starting ~2026-04-20 15:10 UTC.
- Separately, service dashboards show short bursts of 429s from the same customer account around 15:12-15:18 UTC (bursty pattern).
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (text), /v1/embeddings.
- Not global; other customers fine.

Initial reproductions (local):
- curl (from my laptop) using customer API key (redacted) -> sometimes 401, sometimes success.
  curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'

401 sample response (exact):
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found"}

429 sample response (exact):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
 x-rate-limit-limit: 100
 x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
 x-rate-limit-reset: 1618974523
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":23,"message":"Quota exceeded for project"}

Headers we see in logs often:
- x-request-id: abc123-requestid
- forwarded-for / X-Forwarded-For shows customer IP occasionally different from what customer claims (need to verify NATing/edge behaviour)

What I tried so far:
- Verified key existence in admin API (internal/api-keys/validate) -> sometimes returns 200, sometimes 404 for same key (flaky).
  http --auth admin:$ADMIN_TOKEN GET https://internal.redwood/api-keys/{key}/status
- Checked rotation: queried key metadata -> created 2025-12-10, last-rotated null. No automatic rotation configured.
- Checked billing/quotas for account: usage well under committed capacity. No quota limit configured to trigger at these levels.
- Pulled gateway logs (nginx + envoy) for 15:00-15:30 UTC: saw 401 responses originating at auth-service with error code INVALID_KEY_LOOKUP. There are also short 500 spikes from rate-limiter (redis timeouts) during same window.
- Verified Redis cluster metrics: transient CPU/connection bursts at ~15:12; some TIME_WAIT entries.
- Looked at auth-service autoscaling: pods were being cycled (OOMKill) earlier in the day, but not during the window.
- Replayed customer's requests from staging (same key) -> initially failed 401, then immediately worked on retry. Pattern looks like: first request hits 401, quick retry OK, then at high QPS some 429s.

Hypotheses (order is my thinking):
1) Stale cache / eventual consistency of key lookup in auth-service pool: key removed from local cache (or cache node partitioned), causing 401 until cache repopulated from central store. Explains intermittent 401 followed by success on retry.
2) Rate-limit tier mis-configuration: customer has per-route concurrency limit + global token bucket; burst behavior could exhaust x-rate-limit-remaining causing 429s; headers show remaining=0.
3) API key collision / reuse across regions: same key used in two regions; routing sometimes sends traffic to old edge where key not provisioned -> 401.
4) Admin UI / rotation bug: a partial rotation left the key in a limbo state (present in master DB but not replicated to index service).
5) Redis / rate-limiter timeouts causing the token-bucket check to fail open/closed inconsistently -> some requests default to deny (429) or treat as auth failure (401) depending on error path.

Things to validate next (TODOs):
- [ ] Add fine-grained logging around cache miss vs db-lookup failure in auth-service (quick patch to log lookup source) - small PR.
- [ ] Re-run controlled repro from multiple regions (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1) to check routing differences. Use curl with -v and capture X-Edge-Region / Host headers.
- [ ] Dump key cache stats across auth-service pods at the time of incidents (memcache hit/miss).
- [ ] Check key provisioning flow (kafka replication) for lags around 15:00-15:30.
- [ ] Correlate Redis connection errors with 429 timestamps: are the bursts simultaneous?
- [ ] Query api-gateway config for per-route overrides for this account (accidental per-customer throttle).
- [ ] Contact CS to confirm customer-side pattern (did they see retries/clients doing backoff?).

Quick debugging commands I used (notes):
- Check key status via internal API:
  http --auth admin:$ADMIN_TOKEN GET https://internal.redwood/api-keys/{redacted}  # returns 200/404 intermittently
- Search logs for request-id and time window (using loki):
  {app="auth-service"} |~ "INVALID_KEY_LOOKUP" | range 2026-04-20T15:00:00Z to 2026-04-20T15:30:00Z | json
- Count 401 vs 429 in gateway for that key:
  gateway_logs | filter key_id=xxx | stats count(status) by status | last 24h
- Reproduce with verbose curl and save headers:
  curl -v -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}' 2>&1 | tee repro-headers.txt

Notes from an on-call convo with Samir (15:45 UTC):
- Samir: saw a pattern where cache invalidation job fired at 15:11 and a few auth pods restarted -> matches symptom window.
- He suggested temporarily bumping cache TTL to reduce churn while we patch.

Potential quick mitigations:
- Increase cache TTL for API keys from 30s -> 300s (reduce invalidation storm) as a hotfix. Risk: slower revocation; acceptable with CS approval.
- Add a retry-with-backoff in gateway on 401 if key validation failed and upstream responded with transient error (but this hides true invalid key cases).

Next immediate actions (this afternoon):
1) Correlate Kafka lag for "api_keys_provisioned" topic at 15:00-15:20. (Oliver owns infra access)
2) Add more verbose cache-miss logging and roll a canary (one auth pod) to see lookup source.
3) Talk to CS to notify customer of possible short-lived auth cache churn and offer temporary TTL bump.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Did a deploy of auth-service or tooling happen 15:00-15:10? (release-engineering deploys page currently empty)
- Why do some failures produce 401 vs 429? Need to map codepaths.
- Is there a specific proxy/edge returning 401 before auth-service gets the call? Need header traces.

If I get time later: instrument a small synthetic test that simulates cache invalidation and concurrent key lookups to reproduce locally.

End of scratchpad for now. Will update as I get more logs/answers.

-- Lena
(added 2026-04-21 09:12 UTC)
